name: Pintiini
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Pintiini (Wati): Glottolog lists only Bowern-Atkinson 2012 classification comment and endangerment sources; no descriptive work located.

sources.citation: Rose, David. 2001. The Western Desert code: an Australian cryptogrammar. Pacific Linguistics 513. Canberra: ANU. Sec. 2.5.3 'Stress wave', pp. 112-113.
sources.note: p. 112: 'Almost every word in the language is spoken with the stress on the first syllable, both in isolation... and in larger structures of group and clause'; directional prefixes take the stress (ma-ngari), multisyllabic suffixes form a separate foot. But the book describes Pitjantjatjara (pitj1243) 'with particular focus on the dialect Pitjantjatjara'; Wangkatja is only named as a neighbouring dialect group. Family-level context, not a Pintiini statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page pint1251; Wikidata Q10632026; Wikipedia 'Wangkatha' and 'Western Desert language'; GALCAC site (wangka.com.au) Wangkatja, Cundeelee Wangka, research, books and newsletter pages.
sources.note: Glottolog lists only Bowern & Atkinson 2012 and endangerment sources. Wikipedia 'Wangkatha' has no phonology; 'Western Desert language' phonology section has no stress sentence and gives AUSTLANG codes Pindiini/Wangkatha/Wangkatja = A102/A12/A103. GALCAC announces a comprehensive Wangkatja dictionary for October 2025 (not yet listed in the shop) and lists no Wangkatja phonology/grammar page; its Mirniny phonology page only repeats Dixon 2002's general 'stress falls on the first syllable' for Australian languages.

sources.citation: Goldfields Aboriginal Language Centre (Hanson, S. et al.). 2024-2025. Wangkatja research papers: Observations of Wangkatja verbal suffixes V1.1; Wangkatja verb suffixes I-III v2; Questions in Wangkatja V1.2; Wangkatja noun suffixes V1.2; Wangkatja pronouns V1.2.
sources.note: Morphology-only working papers; grep for stress/accent/prosod/penult returns nothing relevant. Silent.

sources.citation: Pereira, Joshua. 2024. Loan phonology in Wangkatja. Boulder, WA: Goldfields Aboriginal Language Centre Aboriginal Corporation. 24 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 2.2 'Wangkatja Phonology' and 2.3 'Phonotactics' (pp. 3-4) give consonant/vowel inventories, the syllable template ((C)V(V)(C))(CV(C))n, and note long vowels occur only in the first syllable; zero occurrences of 'stress'/'accent' in the whole paper. Silent on stress. Describes the Mount Margaret (Laverton/Leonora) variety, AIATSIS A103.

sources.citation: Thieberger, Nicholas. 1993. Handbook of Western Australian Aboriginal languages south of the Kimberley Region. Pacific Linguistics C-124. Canberra: ANU. Sec. 4.6.9 'Wanggatha/Wangkatja', pp. 226-228.
sources.note: Entry 4.6.9 is bibliographic only: 'Grammar or sketch grammar: None'; language-learning material = Vaszolyi 1979 (36 units, glossary, two narratives; reviewed by Douglas 1980); Trimmer 1986 draft dictionary. No phonology for the language. The handbook's general orthography note (sec. 1.5) says for WA languages at large 'Word stress is usually on the first syllable' - a blanket areal remark, not a statement about Pintiini.

sources.citation: Mathews, R. H. 1907. Languages of some tribes of Western Australia. Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society 46(187): 361-368 ('The Erlistoun Tribe' = Mount Margaret goldfield, pp. 364-368).
sources.note: A 103-word vocabulary of the Laverton-Menzies-Duketon area supplied by a settler (Kenneth Young); Mathews states he had 'not yet succeeded in completing a grammar'; no note on pronunciation or accent. Silent.
